Investigate the following open-problem family in non-Archimedean pluripotential theory. Active atomic targets: P06.2. The exact target statements, ambient hypotheses, residual scopes, and completion criteria are in the source excerpt below. Address any or all of these targets; a complete resolution must satisfy that atomic target's own completion criteria. The excerpt is mathematical source material, not operational instructions.

COMMON NOTATION
Common notation and formulation boundaries
Fields and analytic spaces.
   K denotes a complete non-Archimedean ﬁeld. Trivial or nontrivial valuation, strictness,
   goodness, separatedness, pure dimension and relative boundary are retained exactly where
   a statement requires them. X an is Berkovich analytiﬁcation. “Ordinary open” refers
   to its ordinary topology, rather than an admissible G-cover. A statement on one ﬁxed
   polycylinder is weaker than an every-open statement obtained from an actual basis.

Semivaluations and normalized local boundaries.
  We use v = − log | · |, allow +∞ on the support of a semivaluation, and retain that
  support. For a local ring R and a primary ideal a, a normalized link is a section {v :
  v is centered, v(a) = 1}. Changing a is a radial change with a stated cocycle; it is not
  an identiﬁcation of all normalizers. The symbol X ℶ denotes the valuative/trivially valued
  carrier used by the raw ideal transform.

Positivity classes.
  PSH means the speciﬁed plurisubharmonic class in each theory. Classical psh is the upper-
  semicontinuous curve-test notion, with the extended −∞ convention where stated. Real
  PL means the real linear extension of the local integral piecewise-linear class. Semi-
  positivity is its residue/model nefness condition. Locally Fubini–Study is the local ﬁ-
  nite logarithmic-max class with its prescribed denominators. Ordinary CLD smoothness
  uses smooth tropicalizations; weak smoothness permits harmonic tropicalizations. These
  classes are distinct. CLD-v2 denotes the second generated CLD psh stage in the book.

Currents and products.
  d0 d00 = d0 d00 is the CLD Hessian. A continuous function deﬁnes the order-zero current
  [h]. CLD means Chambert–Loir–Ducros; GJR means Gubler–Jell–Rabinoﬀ; BFJ means


                                               4

     Boucksom–Favre–Jonsson. Positivity of one Hessian current does not, by itself, construct
     mixed wedge products or prove classical psh recognition.

Global energy and mass.
  E 1 denotes the ﬁnite-energy class of the named theory. Reference weights, raw intersection
  mass and probability normalization must be ﬁxed before comparing energies or measures.
  Quotienting by R means uniqueness modulo additive constants. Zero top mass cannot be
  divided into a probability measure. The aﬃne-cone probability operator is an explicitly
  separate convention.

Complex singularity data.
         1,1
  α ∈ HBC    (X, R) is a real Bott–Chern class. MP means Mesquita–Piccione, DXZ means
  Darvas–Xia–Zhang, and BJ means Boucksom–Jonsson. I-equivalence records multiplier-
  ideal data; P -equivalence records the ﬁner envelope/singularity data. The latter cannot
  generally be recovered from the former, even at positive mass.

Polyhedral normalization.
   PA denotes piecewise-aﬃne functions. BMPS means Botero–Mazzon–Pille-Schneider. Lit-
   eral integral slopes and the real scalar extension are separate conventions. In dimension
   d, the polyhedral intersection convention diﬀers from the real Alexandrov measure by the
   factor d! and the face multiplicity. Saturated tangent lattices and analytic multiplicities
   are part of an analytic comparison.




FULL FAMILY DOSSIER
5     Recognizing continuous zero-Hessian functions
Active items: P06.2. Status: Open in the residual scope.

5.1    Atomic targets
P06.2 (T2): Recognition of continuous zero-Hessian functions
Let K be complete and nontrivially valued and X good, separated, strict and boundaryless.
Outside the veriﬁed scopes, decide whether every continuous h with d0 d00 [h] = 0 is classically
pluriharmonic (or harmonic where that notion is available), or give a counterexample in this
scope. Scalar ascent of the current equation and regularization of both signs are separate
missing gates. The unrestricted arbitrary-radius product extension is false.

5.2    What constitutes a solution
Prove recognition for general continuous zero-Hessian functions in a new stated scope, or
construct a counterexample satisfying the original strict ambient hypotheses. Make scalar-
current ascent and two-sign regularization separate obligations. Ordinary smooth, weakly
smooth and G-local real-PL conclusions have distinct consequences.

5.3    Full statement and detailed state of the art
The supplied singular descent theorem Book Theorem 18.12.1 settles P06.1: classical plurihar-
monicity implies local real PL regularity throughout the original scope, including arbitrary
singular points. P06.2 retains the reverse bridge from a current equation to the curve-test
notion.
Problem 5.1. Let K be complete and nontrivially valued and let X be a good, separated,
strict, boundaryless K-analytic space. If a continuous h satisﬁes d0 d00 [h] = 0, must h be
classically pluriharmonic, or harmonic under the hypotheses where a classical harmonic notion
is available, outside the positive cases recorded below?
   The residual problem has two logically separate gates. One must ﬁrst control the zero-
current equation after scalar extension, and one must then regularize continuous positive-
current functions into the CLD-psh hierarchy. The next proposition records that these two
gates suﬃce and that every counterexample must obstruct at least one of them.

Proposition 5.1. Let K be complete and nontrivially valued, let X be a good, separated, strict,
boundaryless K-analytic space, and let h : X → R be continuous with d0 d00 [h] = 0. Suppose
that there is an analytic extension L/K such that, for the scalar-extension map π : XL → X
and hL := h ◦ π, the following two conditions hold:
  (1) the current equation ascends, so that d0 d00 [hL ] = 0;

  (2) current positivity regularizes for the two signs of hL : if f ∈ {hL , −hL } and d0 d00 [f ] ≥ 0,
      then f is CLD-psh.
Then h is classically pluriharmonic and locally R-PL. If X is pure-dimensional, then h is also
GJR harmonic.
Corollary 5.2. Let K be complete and nontrivially valued, let X be a good, separated, strict,
boundaryless K-analytic space, and let h : X → R be continuous with d0 d00 [h] = 0. Suppose
that h is not classically pluriharmonic. For every analytic extension L/K, at least one of the
following failures occurs:

                                                 42

 (1) d0 d00 [hL ] 6= 0;

 (2) one of hL and −hL has nonnegative Hessian current but does not belong to the CLD-psh
     hierarchy.

For L = K, the ﬁrst alternative is impossible. Hence every negative answer to P06.2 furnishes,
in one of the two signs of h, a continuous zero-current function outside the CLD-psh hierarchy.
If X is pure-dimensional, this is a counterexample to the converse of Book Proposition 15.9.8
in its stated scope.

    This reduction neither pulls a continuous current through an arbitrary scalar extension
nor proves positive-current regularization. It identiﬁes those operations as distinct proof
obligations and shows that a negative answer to P06.2 produces a zero-current function outside
the CLD-psh hierarchy at the ground ﬁeld. In the pure-dimensional scope this would disprove
the missing nonsmooth converse in Book Proposition 15.9.8.

GJR harmonic. This does not supply locally twisted annular coordinates at the top or insert
annular stages at arbitrary intermediate levels of the tower.
     Annular geometry may also occur at the bottom. The general transfer statement Book
Proposition M.1.34 isolates the common exact descent, classical-pluriharmonic transfer, R-
harmonic transfer, and ﬁrst-current-rigidity transfer of the four allowed bundle types over an
arbitrary admissible base. Applying it to a globally coordinated curve-polyannulus product
gives Book Corollary M.1.53: after any such mixed tower, the top function still has the
unique logarithmic coeﬃcient formula over the original curve. Applying it instead to a locally
trivial curve-polyannulus bundle or a locally trivial mixed curve-polycylinder bundle gives
Book Corollary M.1.54, Book Corollary M.1.55, with classical pluriharmonicity, local R-PL
regularity, and GJR harmonicity but no global coeﬃcient formula. Thus locally twisted
annular coordinates are now allowed at the bottom of the mixed exact tower. The result
still requires their displayed analytic local trivializations and does not allow an annular stage
to be interleaved at an arbitrary later level, an annular ﬁbration without such charts, or an
arbitrary nonproduct germ.
     For globally coordinated annular products, the two endpoint orders can be fully interleaved.
In Book Theorem M.1.20, each stage of a ﬁnite boundaryless tower over the curve may be
either one of the four exact bundle types or a globally coordinated ﬁnite standard strict
open-polyannulus product. An induction preserves classical pluriharmonicity, R-harmonicity,
and ﬁrst-current rigidity at every level. It gives a unique normal form on the tower top
with one logarithmic term for every annular coordinate introduced anywhere in the tower;
the zero-current base coeﬃcient and all locally constant slope coeﬃcients live on the original
curve. Thus globally coordinated annular stages may now occur at arbitrary levels. For a
global normal form, the remaining obstruction is the transition monodromy of locally twisted
annulus bundles: the theorem does not choose global annular coordinates. For one locally
trivial polyannulus bundle over the curve, however, Book Proposition M.1.26 now identiﬁes the
coeﬃcient system on overlaps. The logarithmic coordinates transform by a locally constant
unimodular integer matrix and a vector of zero-current base functions. These data satisfy
the aﬃne cocycle law, deﬁne a rank-s local system of lattices, and make the local slope
vectors of every zero-current function a global parallel section of its dual real local system.
Thus the monodromy defect is encoded intrinsically even when it is not trivialized. The
remaining translation defect is measured exactly by the zero-current radiance class of Book
Deﬁnition M.1.1. Book Proposition M.1.27 makes its vanishing equivalent to a purely linear
overlap law after zero-current aﬃne gauge and then gives one global coeﬃcient formula for
every zero-current function. The gauges are not asserted to be logarithms of analytic units,
so this criterion does not manufacture global annular coordinates. Even when the full class
does not vanish, Book Proposition M.1.28 gives the exact residual answer slope by slope: the
slopes of global zero-current functions are precisely the parallel dual sections whose scalar
contraction with the radiance class vanishes. Its exact sequence also shows that an injective
contraction, and in particular the absence of parallel dual sections, forces unique descent of
every zero-current function to the original curve. When the radiance class vanishes, a chosen
aﬃne gauge splits this sequence.

every annular stage after base change. On each member of the cover, the whole restricted
tower is an instance of the interleaved theorem; the local conclusions therefore glue even
though the annular coordinates, radii, and product trivializations need not agree on overlaps.

deliberately gives no global coeﬃcient formula. It also does not treat annular trivializations
available only over arbitrary opens of intermediate tower levels, because such opens need not

COMMON NOTATION
Common notation and formulation boundaries
Fields and analytic spaces.
   K denotes a complete non-Archimedean ﬁeld. Trivial or nontrivial valuation, strictness,
   goodness, separatedness, pure dimension and relative boundary are retained exactly where

   polycylinder is weaker than an every-open statement obtained from an actual basis.

Semivaluations and normalized local boundaries.
  We use v = − log | · |, allow +∞ on the support of a semivaluation, and retain that
  support. For a local ring R and a primary ideal a, a normalized link is a section {v :
  v is centered, v(a) = 1}. Changing a is a radial change with a stated cocycle; it is not

  carrier used by the raw ideal transform.

  semicontinuous curve-test notion, with the extended −∞ convention where stated. Real
  PL means the real linear extension of the local integral piecewise-linear class. Semi-
  positivity is its residue/model nefness condition. Locally Fubini–Study is the local ﬁ-
  nite logarithmic-max class with its prescribed denominators. Ordinary CLD smoothness
  uses smooth tropicalizations; weak smoothness permits harmonic tropicalizations. These
  classes are distinct. CLD-v2 denotes the second generated CLD psh stage in the book.

         1,1

Let K be complete and nontrivially valued and X good, separated, strict and boundaryless.
Outside the veriﬁed scopes, decide whether every continuous h with d0 d00 [h] = 0 is classically
pluriharmonic (or harmonic where that notion is available), or give a counterexample in this

singular points. P06.2 retains the reverse bridge from a current equation to the curve-test

strict, boundaryless K-analytic space. If a continuous h satisﬁes d0 d00 [h] = 0, must h be

and hL := h ◦ π, the following two conditions hold:
  (1) the current equation ascends, so that d0 d00 [hL ] = 0;

  (2) current positivity regularizes for the two signs of hL : if f ∈ {hL , −hL } and d0 d00 [f ] ≥ 0,

GJR harmonic.

boundaryless K-analytic space, and let h : X → R be continuous with d0 d00 [h] = 0. Suppose

following failures occurs:

notes.detailedSummary: For every complete nontrivially valued K, every algebraic valued M/K with completion L, and every actual good separated strict boundaryless pure n-dimensional X, n>=1, the draft proves ordinary d′d″[h]=0 iff d′d″[h_L]=0 for finite continuous h against every compact ordinary complementary test. notes.text:
The new deliverable is an unconditional, but unverified, complete proof draft of the requested completed-algebraic current-transport gate. It is partial progress on original P06.2, not classical recognition.

Precisely, let K be any complete nontrivially valued field, M/K any algebraic valued extension, L its completion, and X any actual good separated strict boundaryless K-analytic space pure of analytic dimension n≥1. Singularities and nilpotents are retained. For every finite continuous real h, with π:X_L→X, the draft proves

    d'd''[h]=0 ⇔ d'd''[h∘π]=0,

against ALL compact ordinary smooth (n−1,n−1) tests. No separability, tameness, perfectness, unit separation, Radon-Hessian, psh assumption, blanket invariant-form descent, current pullback, or curve reduction is imposed. It also proves exact compact-test descent in every bidegree: for good separated strict X and every β∈A_c^{a,b}(X_L), one finite embedded E⊆M and α_E∈A_c^{a,b}(X_E) satisfy β=q_E^*α_E as ordinary smooth sections. This subsidiary statement needs no purity or boundarylessness.

The authoritative proof is P06.2-argument.md, with standalone P06.2-partial.tex and twice-compiled P06.2-partial.pdf, in /workspace/research/campaigns/round-21/P06.2-all-dimensional-completed-algebraic-continuation/artifacts/codex-ZwIWCf. The Markdown contains all supporting proofs and 33 complete selected primary bodies with their printed proof endings. status.json has exactly id,status,exact_result,proof_file,concrete_gaps, with id=P06.2, status=partial, and proof_file=P06.2-argument.md. The original task, completion criteria, and assignment are preserved verbatim in original-task.json, original-problem.txt, completion-criteria.txt, and assignment-verbatim.txt. No earlier theorem, review verdict, or catalogue description is a premise.

Here is the checking chain. Write D=d'd'', t_f=−log|f|, and B_h(α)=∫h(Dα)_Rad; vanishing of B_h on all complementary tests is the current equation, up to its fixed irrelevant duality sign. D[h] is not assumed Radon. Only differentiated smooth top forms are measures.

The analytic imports are exact restricted primary statements. CLD arXiv:1204.6277v2, 25 July 2025, §§11.1.1–10 and 11.4.4 gives compact Hausdorff affinoid spectra, noetherian actual algebras with closed ideals, surjectivity onto prime spectra, residue fields as completions of kernel-quotient fraction fields, rational domains and their universal analytic-domain property, completed scalar tensors and surjective scalar projections, and finite-module affinoid topology. Section 11.1.5 specifically gives a rational neighborhood inside any ordinary open with every defining inequality strict at the point. Section 11.7.7 gives strict affinoid neighborhoods in good strict spaces over nontrivially valued fields. Section 11.2.3 gives complete scalar TOTAL dimension invariance, domain LOCAL dimension invariance, strict-affinoid Krull dimension, and the local maximum over minimal components; it does not by itself give purity. Separatedness gives Hausdorffness by 11.2.2. Berkovich, Publ. Math. IHES 78 (1993), Proposition 1.5.5(i),(iii),(iv), gives ordinary relative interiors of domains and base-change inclusion for relative interiors. CLD 11.4.1 gives composition equality when the middle morphism is locally separated. These check boundarylessness, including the locally lifted finite constant field.

CLD 6.2.1–2 and Proposition 15.1.1(b) give ordinary sheaves of forms with unit-moment descriptions on ORDINARY open covers, in every bidegree. CLD 3.3.3 and Lemma 1.9.4 give ambient smooth coefficient representatives, the latter used only when its paralinear subset is closed in its ambient open. CLD 3.3.10–12 gives wedge and both derivations and their smooth functoriality. Proposition 3.4.4 says a represented form is zero in the G-form sheaf exactly when its coefficient restriction is zero on the image of EVERY compact domain. Ordinary smooth forms are the corresponding sections having ordinary local descriptions. Numerical-zero smooth scalar sections are therefore zero sections, proved by this compact-image criterion. CLD 15.2.2 and Corollary 15.2.5 give compact cutoffs in our good Hausdorff scope; the finite partition is explicitly constructed below. The broad 15.2.9 assertion is not used.

Ducros, Confluentes Math. 4 (2012), 1250007, Theorem 3.2(1), states that a tuple of analytic units on compact Γ-strict analytic dimension d has a c-polytope norm image of dimension AT MOST d, with c=(Q,(|K*|Γ)^Q). Here Γ={1}. No universal equality from CLD 12.2.4 is used. CLD 5.4.4, 14.1.8 and 14.1.12 provide pleasant compact charts and compatible cell refinements. CLD 14.2.2, 14.3.2–5 and 14.5.1–2 give positive constant calibrations from actual finite-flat moment degrees, summed over skeletal sheets. CLD 5.8.1–5 gives domain-compatible top-form measures from their skeletal densities; 5.10.1(c),(d) gives their pleasant-chart integration formula. Lower-dimensional cells have no top measure. CLD 15.7.1–2 supplies the level-n tropical structure and domain compatibility on Hausdorff pure spaces; 7.3.5 defines continuous multiplier currents. Stokes 5.11.1(a) applies to arbitrary compact (n−1,n) forms, with the double-prime version obtained by J. The symmetry-restricted Green formula is not used.

Two normalizations are kept separate. CLD 14.3.6 and 15.3.1 give π_*((π*ω)_Rad,L)=ω_Rad,K for locally integrable top forms under complete scalar extension, with NO degree factor. CLD Remark 14.4.3 instead gives μ_K=[F:K]μ_F for the SAME CARRIER of an F-space viewed over K. The latter comparison is used only after proving its actual F-analytic structure and common unit/form sheaves.

FINITE SUPPORTING MATHEMATICS. For any actual affinoid Banach A and finite E/K, A completed-tensor E=A tensor E with finite-module topology. A basis of a finite-dimensional normed space gives an equivalent coefficient maximum norm: induct on dimension, using completeness and closedness of the preceding span and positive distance of the last vector. Its bounded coefficient maps tensor with A and identify the tensor topology with complete A^[E:K]. This retains nilpotents. Finite extending absolute values are unique by comparing equivalent norms on powers and taking roots. A finite separable field has degree-many embeddings; a linear combination of generators separating them exists because finitely many nonzero polynomial conditions cannot exhaust the infinite field K. It is primitive. Extending embeddings successively into a normal closure proves the usual fixed-field and subgroup facts. In particular E/E^H has group H and degree |H|, by its primitive element's H-orbit polynomial.

For finite Galois E/K, tensoring the finite linear kernel equations for E^G=K yields (A⊗E)^G=A without averaging in K. Thus N(f)=∏g gf and its inverse are actual downstairs units. The point fibre over x, C=H(x), is M(C⊗E), a finite product of fields. G acts transitively; multiple orbits would give a nontrivial invariant idempotent in C. For the actual stabilizer H of y, invariant tuples give D_y^H=C for its field factor D_y. A primitive b gives D_y=C[b] and exactly |H| distinct H-conjugates, so D_y/C is Galois of degree |H|. Hence E^H embeds in H(x).

Finite componentwise purity is checked directly. For a strict affinoid A in pure n-dimensional X, a point with each minimal-prime kernel P lies on that component alone; therefore dim(A/P)=n. For separable E, A_red embeds into the product of its minimal-component fraction fields; tensoring with E is algebraically exact and those field tensors are reduced. Each upstairs minimal prime is consequently one of the field-factor kernels and contracts to a minimal P. Its quotient is finite integral over A/P with zero kernel, and dimension n. The integral dimension argument is supplied: the finite-module determinant/Nakayama argument proves lying over, quotienting proves going up, and localizing a quotient domain to a finite domain over a field proves incomparability. For purely inseparable E of exponent q, each b∈A⊗E has b^q∈A. Prime membership b∈Q iff b^q∈P uniquely describes the prime over P and preserves chains; minimal components and dimensions agree. Actual algebras, not reductions, are used for all measures.

A separable residue constant is lifted on an actual neighborhood. For primitive a∈H(x), monic P=∑p_jT^j, approximate a by an analytic fraction g=f/b, retaining b invertible on a strict rational neighborhood. Choose R∈|K*|>max(1,|a|), 0<d∈|K*|<|P'(a)|, M_0=max({1}∪{|p_j|R^(j−2):j≥2}), and small c∈|K*| with s=c/d<min(1,R) and v=M_0c/d²<1. Approximate so |g(x)|<R, |P(g)(x)|<c, |P'(g)(x)|>d and |g(x)−a|<s. The quotient rational Tate algebra imposing |g|≤R, |P(g)|≤c, |P'(g)|≥d gives ACTUAL Banach bounds ||g||≤R, ||P(g)||≤c and ||P'(g)^−1||≤d^−1. Binomial expansion gives quadratic remainder ≤M_0||w||² and derivative change ≤M_0||w||. Newton increments shrink by factor v, and Neumann inversion preserves the derivative bound; completeness gives a root z. Two roots within s of g(x) have difference multiplied by P'(g(x))+w, |w|≤M_0s<d, so z(x)=a. Thus F=K[a] embeds boundedly in the actual affinoid algebra.

For this bounded finite-field action, the equivalent norm ||b||_F=sup_{u∈F*}||ub||_A/|u| is complete, F-homogeneous and submultiplicative. The strict K-Tate presentation extends to a bounded surjection from the F-Tate algebra; uniform lifts through the K-presentation prove equivalence with the quotient norm. Spectra agree by finite norm uniqueness, rational algebras agree by their universal presentations, and common unit moments and compact-image nullity identify all ordinary forms. Goodness, strictness, purity and separatedness over F follow from these actual algebras and the closed F-diagonal. Interior composition for U→M(F)→M(K) makes the chosen ordinary U boundaryless over F. Same-carrier calibration gives B_h,K=[F:K]B_h,F, a cancellable positive REAL integer.

Now induct simultaneously on |Gal(E/K)|. The G-fixed locus S is closed. At y∉S, F=E^H has the preceding local lift; its group H is smaller. Actual tensor identities F⊗K E=∏_{τ:F→E}E and A⊗K E=∏τ A⊗_{F,τ}E follow from distinct linear factors and retain all nilpotents and finite-module topologies. These are actual open-and-closed components with smaller conjugate Galois groups. Induction gives zero current near y; finite compact partitions kill every test supported off S.

At y∈S, its whole fibre is singleton. Compact-complement shrinking gives a strict downstairs V whose full V_E lies in the upstairs test's unit-description open and all its translates. Use orbit moment t=(t_gf_i), fixed linear subspace W and real averaging projection P_0. Averaged coordinates equal |G|^−1 t_N(f_i)∘p_E. Shrink so both t(V_E) and P_0t(V_E) lie in the coefficient open, and extend the coefficient form ω globally by a Euclidean bump. Then ω_0=P_0* i*ω restricts to ω on W and is represented by a downstairs norm-unit form. Downstairs compact cutoffs θ_i near the image of S∩supp β split β into a remainder off S, matched pullback tests killed by canonical measure projection, and errors γ_i with coefficient restriction zero on W (times the full space of any extra cutoff coordinates).

The full tensor collar estimate kills those errors. For e_δ=χ(Qt/δ)γ, Q=1−P_0, supports lie in one compact C. The complementary test (1−χ(Qt/δ))γ is supported off S, giving B_hE(γ)=B_hE(e_δ) exactly. On a compact n-cell let r=rank(Q on its tangent). Collar volume is O(δ^r), by splitting the affine tangent into its W part and a transverse complement. This remains valid for boundary-face-only contact. If its affine span misses W, the collar is eventually empty; rank zero gives exact zero restriction. For r≥2, the two-derivative O(δ^−2) bound gives uniformly bounded L1 differentiated coefficients. For r=1, d't∧d''t kills every complementary exterior component containing either transverse generator. The sole surviving coefficient A(u,t) has A(u,0)=0 by restriction-zero on W, hence A=O(t). Second-cutoff terms are O(δ^−1), as are first-cutoff terms, and O(δ) volume gives a uniform bound. Undifferentiated L1 coefficients tend to zero.

Actual positive sheet weights give ||(t*ζ)_Rad||_TV≤∑σ cσ∫σ||ζ restricted to Tσ||, with fixed finite positive constants including every Artinian fibre length. This proves uniform TV of De_δ BEFORE any signed pushforward. For a fixed compact smooth scalar a, two Stokes steps give ∫aDe_δ=∫e_δ∧Da without symmetry assumptions. Add a's unit coordinates to the JOINT moment; restriction-zero persists on W times the added space, and the undifferentiated L1 estimate gives weak convergence to zero. Euclidean bump extensions near compact joint images justify the off-cell comparison points. This refinement may depend on a; the differentiated TV bound does not. Compact smooth approximation |a−h_E|<ε on C then gives limsup|∫h_E De_δ|≤C_1ε. Let ε→0. This completes finite-Galois ascent for arbitrary complementary forms. Reverse transport uses canonical measure projection, never field-degree division.

For finite separable E/K, take a genuine finite Galois normal closure N containing E. Ascent to N and canonical top-measure descent through N/E prove ascent to E. For finite purely inseparable exponent q, scalar projection is a homeomorphism: all values upstairs are forced by |b|=|b^q downstairs|^(1/q), and projection is surjective. On a full downstairs affinoid neighborhood within an upstairs moment chart, both f_j^q and (f_j^−1)^q lie in the actual downstairs algebra, hence g_j=f_j^q is an actual unit. The moment identity t_f=q^−1 t_g∘p gives all-bidegree descent by pulling coefficients back under t↦t/q; a (a,b) exterior term is scaled by q^−(a+b). Finite compact partitions give every compact complementary test, so canonical projection proves the current equation. In characteristic p, write each generator's irreducible polynomial as g_i(T^(p^r_i)) with g_i'≠0. The embedded S=K(a_i^(p^r_i)) is finite separable and E/S purely inseparable of one common exponent. Thus the ACTUAL tower K⊆S⊆E gives arbitrary mixed finite stages; characteristic zero is separable. No preceding finite, curve, or inseparable result was granted.

NEW COMPLETION STEP. The image of A⊗M is dense in A completed-tensor L by approximating the finitely many L-coefficients in each tensor in actual Banach norm. For finite E, bounded basis-coordinate maps give the actual associative isomorphism (A_E) completed-tensor_E L=A_L. No injection of an infinite algebraic tensor or completed preservation of arbitrary injections is assumed. Scalar surjectivity can be proved directly by embedding M into an algebraic closure of H(x), using the compatible unique finite norms, completing it, and extending evaluation to A_L via the full tensor bound for every representation. Compact scalar inverse images follow by covering a downstairs compact with finitely many affinoid ordinary interiors; its preimage is closed in their compact scalar extensions.

For a rational R_L with |f_i|≤r_i|g| and no common zero, let δ=min max(|g|,r_i^−1|f_i|)>0 on the ambient compact affinoid. Approximate g,f_i at one finite stage with errors <δ and <r_iδ. When |g|≥δ, denominator norm is unchanged; each numerator at or above its threshold has unchanged norm, while one below stays strictly below. Thus weak/strict comparisons and equality boundaries are unchanged. When |g|<δ some weighted numerator is ≥δ, stays unchanged, and makes both full systems false for the approximants too. This proves equality of the entire rational domain and its strict locus, including every equality locus within the validity domain; it does not falsely assert preservation of irrelevant individual equalities outside it. Surjectivity makes the approximants have no common zero downstairs, hence generate the unit ideal. The universal analytic-domain property identifies R_L=(R_E)_L with its ACTUAL rational algebra. The strict locus O_E is ordinary open and has full inverse image precisely O_L. These specific presentation neighborhoods, not arbitrary absolute interiors, are the needed ordinary interiors. Rational-neighborhood bases place them inside any given upstairs description open.

On such a compact R_L inside a form-description open, approximate each unit f_j by u_j from one finite R_E with Banach error <min|f_j|. Then |u_j|=|f_j| EXACTLY on all R_L. Surjectivity implies u_j is an actual unit on R_E, and the finite-stage moment image equals the upstairs moment image, so the same Euclidean coefficient domain is valid. The smooth scalar logarithm of f_j/u_j is numerical zero, hence the zero SECTION by compact-image nullity. Applying each derivation identifies both d't_fj and d''t_fj with the corresponding pulled-back unit differentials. Substitution in every term ω_IJ(t_f)d't_f,I∧d''t_f,J produces a stage form b_E with β=q_E*b_E on the entire saturated ordinary open, including zero regions. This is exact all-bidegree descent, not C0 approximation of differentiated forms.

Cover compact supp β by finitely many such saturated opens, enlarge to one finite E, and apply a compact partition θ_i at E near q_E(supp β), with supports compactly contained in their definition opens. Put α_E=∑ zero-extension(θ_i b_i,E). Each extension is ordinary smooth because its support is a compact closed subset inside the open. On the WHOLE upstairs space its pullback is (∑q_E*θ_i)β=β: the sum is one near supp β and β is zero elsewhere. No original-support saturation or stage-overlap agreement is assumed. Compact support is a finite union of cutoff supports. This explicitly proves arbitrary higher-form compact gluing rather than importing it from a scalar lemma.

Common notation and formulation boundaries

  PL means the real linear extension of the local integral piecewise-linear class. Semi-
  positivity is its residue/model nefness condition. Locally Fubini–Study is the local ﬁ-

The new deliverable is an unconditional, but unverified, complete proof draft of the requested completed-algebraic current-transport gate. It is partial progress on original P06.2, not classical recognition.

Precisely, let K be any complete nontrivially valued field, M/K any algebraic valued extension, L its completion, and X any actual good separated strict boundaryless K-analytic space pure of analytic dimension n≥1. Singularities and nilpotents are retained. For every finite continuous real h, with π:X_L→X, the draft proves

    d'd''[h]=0 ⇔ d'd''[h∘π]=0,

against ALL compact ordinary smooth (n−1,n−1) tests. No separability, tameness, perfectness, unit separation, Radon-Hessian, psh assumption, blanket invariant-form descent, current pullback, or curve reduction is imposed. It also proves exact compact-test descent in every bidegree: for good separated strict X and every β∈A_c^{a,b}(X_L), one finite embedded E⊆M and α_E∈A_c^{a,b}(X_E) satisfy β=q_E^*α_E as ordinary smooth sections. This subsidiary statement needs no purity or boundarylessness.

The authoritative proof is P06.2-argument.md, with standalone P06.2-partial.tex and twice-compiled P06.2-partial.pdf, in /workspace/research/campaigns/round-21/P06.2-all-dimensional-completed-algebraic-continuation/artifacts/codex-ZwIWCf. The Markdown contains all supporting proofs and 33 complete selected primary bodies with their printed proof endings. status.json has exactly id,status,exact_result,proof_file,concrete_gaps, with id=P06.2, status=partial, and proof_file=P06.2-argument.md. The original task, completion criteria, and assignment are preserved verbatim in original-task.json, original-problem.txt, completion-criteria.txt, and assignment-verbatim.txt. No earlier theorem, review verdict, or catalogue description is a premise.

Here is the checking chain. Write D=d'd'', t_f=−log|f|, and B_h(α)=∫h(Dα)_Rad; vanishing of B_h on all complementary tests is the current equation, up to its fixed irrelevant duality sign. D[h] is not assumed Radon. Only differentiated smooth top forms are measures.

The analytic imports are exact restricted primary statements. CLD arXiv:1204.6277v2, 25 July 2025, §§11.1.1–10 and 11.4.4 gives compact Hausdorff affinoid spectra, noetherian actual algebras with closed ideals, surjectivity onto prime spectra, residue fields as completions of kernel-quotient fraction fields, rational domains and their universal analytic-domain property, completed scalar tensors and surjective scalar projections, and finite-module affinoid topology. Section 11.1.5 specifically gives a rational neighborhood inside any ordinary open with every defining inequality strict at the point. Section 11.7.7 gives strict affinoid neighborhoods in good strict spaces over nontrivially valued fields. Section 11.2.3 gives complete scalar TOTAL dimension invariance, domain LOCAL dimension invariance, strict-affinoid Krull dimension, and the local maximum over minimal components; it does not by itself give purity. Separatedness gives Hausdorffness by 11.2.2. Berkovich, Publ. Math. IHES 78 (1993), Proposition 1.5.5(i),(iii),(iv), gives ordinary relative interiors of domains and base-change inclusion for relative interiors. CLD 11.4.1 gives composition equality when the middle morphism is locally separated. These check boundarylessness, including the locally lifted finite constant field.

CLD 6.2.1–2 and Proposition 15.1.1(b) give ordinary sheaves of forms with unit-moment descriptions on ORDINARY open covers, in every bidegree. CLD 3.3.3 and Lemma 1.9.4 give ambient smooth coefficient representatives, the latter used only when its paralinear subset is closed in its ambient open. CLD 3.3.10–12 gives wedge and both derivations and their smooth functoriality. Proposition 3.4.4 says a represented form is zero in the G-form sheaf exactly when its coefficient restriction is zero on the image of EVERY compact domain. Ordinary smooth forms are the corresponding sections having ordinary local descriptions. Numerical-zero smooth scalar sections are therefore zero sections, proved by this compact-image criterion. CLD 15.2.2 and Corollary 15.2.5 give compact cutoffs in our good Hausdorff scope; the finite partition is explicitly constructed below. The broad 15.2.9 assertion is not used.

Ducros, Confluentes Math. 4 (2012), 1250007, Theorem 3.2(1), states that a tuple of analytic units on compact Γ-strict analytic dimension d has a c-polytope norm image of dimension AT MOST d, with c=(Q,(|K*|Γ)^Q). Here Γ={1}. No universal equality from CLD 12.2.4 is used. CLD 5.4.4, 14.1.8 and 14.1.12 provide pleasant compact charts and compatible cell refinements. CLD 14.2.2, 14.3.2–5 and 14.5.1–2 give positive constant calibrations from actual finite-flat moment degrees, summed over skeletal sheets. CLD 5.8.1–5 gives domain-compatible top-form measures from their skeletal densities; 5.10.1(c),(d) gives their pleasant-chart integration formula. Lower-dimensional cells have no top measure. CLD 15.7.1–2 supplies the level-n tropical structure and domain compatibility on Hausdorff pure spaces; 7.3.5 defines continuous multiplier currents. Stokes 5.11.1(a) applies to arbitrary compact (n−1,n) forms, with the double-prime version obtained by J. The symmetry-restricted Green formula is not used.

Two normalizations are kept separate. CLD 14.3.6 and 15.3.1 give π_*((π*ω)_Rad,L)=ω_Rad,K for locally integrable top forms under complete scalar extension, with NO degree factor. CLD Remark 14.4.3 instead gives μ_K=[F:K]μ_F for the SAME CARRIER of an F-space viewed over K. The latter comparison is used only after proving its actual F-analytic structure and common unit/form sheaves.

FINITE SUPPORTING MATHEMATICS. For any actual affinoid Banach A and finite E/K, A completed-tensor E=A tensor E with finite-module topology. A basis of a finite-dimensional normed space gives an equivalent coefficient maximum norm: induct on dimension, using completeness and closedness of the preceding span and positive distance of the last vector. Its bounded coefficient maps tensor with A and identify the tensor topology with complete A^[E:K]. This retains nilpotents. Finite extending absolute values are unique by comparing equivalent norms on powers and taking roots. A finite separable field has degree-many embeddings; a linear combination of generators separating them exists because finitely many nonzero polynomial conditions cannot exhaust the infinite field K. It is primitive. Extending embeddings successively into a normal closure proves the usual fixed-field and subgroup facts. In particular E/E^H has group H and degree |H|, by its primitive element's H-orbit polynomial.

For finite Galois E/K, tensoring the finite linear kernel equations for E^G=K yields (A⊗E)^G=A without averaging in K. Thus N(f)=∏g gf and its inverse are actual downstairs units. The point fibre over x, C=H(x), is M(C⊗E), a finite product of fields. G acts transitively; multiple orbits would give a nontrivial invariant idempotent in C. For the actual stabilizer H of y, invariant tuples give D_y^H=C for its field factor D_y. A primitive b gives D_y=C[b] and exactly |H| distinct H-conjugates, so D_y/C is Galois of degree |H|. Hence E^H embeds in H(x).

Finite componentwise purity is checked directly. For a strict affinoid A in pure n-dimensional X, a point with each minimal-prime kernel P lies on that component alone; therefore dim(A/P)=n. For separable E, A_red embeds into the product of its minimal-component fraction fields; tensoring with E is algebraically exact and those field tensors are reduced. Each upstairs minimal prime is consequently one of the field-factor kernels and contracts to a minimal P. Its quotient is finite integral over A/P with zero kernel, and dimension n. The integral dimension argument is supplied: the finite-module determinant/Nakayama argument proves lying over, quotienting proves going up, and localizing a quotient domain to a finite domain over a field proves incomparability. For purely inseparable E of exponent q, each b∈A⊗E has b^q∈A. Prime membership b∈Q iff b^q∈P uniquely describes the prime over P and preserves chains; minimal components and dimensions agree. Actual algebras, not reductions, are used for all measures.

A separable residue constant is lifted on an actual neighborhood. For primitive a∈H(x), monic P=∑p_jT^j, approximate a by an analytic fraction g=f/b, retaining b invertible on a strict rational neighborhood. Choose R∈|K*|>max(1,|a|), 0<d∈|K*|<|P'(a)|, M_0=max({1}∪{|p_j|R^(j−2):j≥2}), and small c∈|K*| with s=c/d<min(1,R) and v=M_0c/d²<1. Approximate so |g(x)|<R, |P(g)(x)|<c, |P'(g)(x)|>d and |g(x)−a|<s. The quotient rational Tate algebra imposing |g|≤R, |P(g)|≤c, |P'(g)|≥d gives ACTUAL Banach bounds ||g||≤R, ||P(g)||≤c and ||P'(g)^−1||≤d^−1. Binomial expansion gives quadratic remainder ≤M_0||w||² and derivative change ≤M_0||w||. Newton increments shrink by factor v, and Neumann inversion preserves the derivative bound; completeness gives a root z. Two roots within s of g(x) have difference multiplied by P'(g(x))+w, |w|≤M_0s<d, so z(x)=a. Thus F=K[a] embeds boundedly in the actual affinoid algebra.

For this bounded finite-field action, the equivalent norm ||b||_F=sup_{u∈F*}||ub||_A/|u| is complete, F-homogeneous and submultiplicative. The strict K-Tate presentation extends to a bounded surjection from the F-Tate algebra; uniform lifts through the K-presentation prove equivalence with the quotient norm. Spectra agree by finite norm uniqueness, rational algebras agree by their universal presentations, and common unit moments and compact-image nullity identify all ordinary forms. Goodness, strictness, purity and separatedness over F follow from these actual algebras and the closed F-diagonal. Interior composition for U→M(F)→M(K) makes the chosen ordinary U boundaryless over F. Same-carrier calibration gives B_h,K=[F:K]B_h,F, a cancellable positive REAL integer.

Now induct simultaneously on |Gal(E/K)|. The G-fixed locus S is closed. At y∉S, F=E^H has the preceding local lift; its group H is smaller. Actual tensor identities F⊗K E=∏_{τ:F→E}E and A⊗K E=∏τ A⊗_{F,τ}E follow from distinct linear factors and retain all nilpotents and finite-module topologies. These are actual open-and-closed components with smaller conjugate Galois groups. Induction gives zero current near y; finite compact partitions kill every test supported off S.

At y∈S, its whole fibre is singleton. Compact-complement shrinking gives a strict downstairs V whose full V_E lies in the upstairs test's unit-description open and all its translates. Use orbit moment t=(t_gf_i), fixed linear subspace W and real averaging projection P_0. Averaged coordinates equal |G|^−1 t_N(f_i)∘p_E. Shrink so both t(V_E) and P_0t(V_E) lie in the coefficient open, and extend the coefficient form ω globally by a Euclidean bump. Then ω_0=P_0* i*ω restricts to ω on W and is represented by a downstairs norm-unit form. Downstairs compact cutoffs θ_i near the image of S∩supp β split β into a remainder off S, matched pullback tests killed by canonical measure projection, and errors γ_i with coefficient restriction zero on W (times the full space of any extra cutoff coordinates).

The full tensor collar estimate kills those errors. For e_δ=χ(Qt/δ)γ, Q=1−P_0, supports lie in one compact C. The complementary test (1−χ(Qt/δ))γ is supported off S, giving B_hE(γ)=B_hE(e_δ) exactly. On a compact n-cell let r=rank(Q on its tangent). Collar volume is O(δ^r), by splitting the affine tangent into its W part and a transverse complement. This remains valid for boundary-face-only contact. If its affine span misses W, the collar is eventually empty; rank zero gives exact zero restriction. For r≥2, the two-derivative O(δ^−2) bound gives uniformly bounded L1 differentiated coefficients. For r=1, d't∧d''t kills every complementary exterior component containing either transverse generator. The sole surviving coefficient A(u,t) has A(u,0)=0 by restriction-zero on W, hence A=O(t). Second-cutoff terms are O(δ^−1), as are first-cutoff terms, and O(δ) volume gives a uniform bound. Undifferentiated L1 coefficients tend to zero.

Actual positive sheet weights give ||(t*ζ)_Rad||_TV≤∑σ cσ∫σ||ζ restricted to Tσ||, with fixed finite positive constants including every Artinian fibre length. This proves uniform TV of De_δ BEFORE any signed pushforward. For a fixed compact smooth scalar a, two Stokes steps give ∫aDe_δ=∫e_δ∧Da without symmetry assumptions. Add a's unit coordinates to the JOINT moment; restriction-zero persists on W times the added space, and the undifferentiated L1 estimate gives weak convergence to zero. Euclidean bump extensions near compact joint images justify the off-cell comparison points. This refinement may depend on a; the differentiated TV bound does not. Compact smooth approximation |a−h_E|<ε on C then gives limsup|∫h_E De_δ|≤C_1ε. Let ε→0. This completes finite-Galois ascent for arbitrary complementary forms. Reverse transport uses canonical measure projection, never field-degree division.

For finite separable E/K, take a genuine finite Galois normal closure N containing E. Ascent to N and canonical top-measure descent through N/E prove ascent to E. For finite purely inseparable exponent q, scalar projection is a homeomorphism: all values upstairs are forced by |b|=|b^q downstairs|^(1/q), and projection is surjective. On a full downstairs affinoid neighborhood within an upstairs moment chart, both f_j^q and (f_j^−1)^q lie in the actual downstairs algebra, hence g_j=f_j^q is an actual unit. The moment identity t_f=q^−1 t_g∘p gives all-bidegree descent by pulling coefficients back under t↦t/q; a (a,b) exterior term is scaled by q^−(a+b). Finite compact partitions give every compact complementary test, so canonical projection proves the current equation. In characteristic p, write each generator's irreducible polynomial as g_i(T^(p^r_i)) with g_i'≠0. The embedded S=K(a_i^(p^r_i)) is finite separable and E/S purely inseparable of one common exponent. Thus the ACTUAL tower K⊆S⊆E gives arbitrary mixed finite stages; characteristic zero is separable. No preceding finite, curve, or inseparable result was granted.

NEW COMPLETION STEP. The image of A⊗M is dense in A completed-tensor L by approximating the finitely many L-coefficients in each tensor in actual Banach norm. For finite E, bounded basis-coordinate maps give the actual associative isomorphism (A_E) completed-tensor_E L=A_L. No injection of an infinite algebraic tensor or completed preservation of arbitrary injections is assumed. Scalar surjectivity can be proved directly by embedding M into an algebraic closure of H(x), using the compatible unique finite norms, completing it, and extending evaluation to A_L via the full tensor bound for every representation. Compact scalar inverse images follow by covering a downstairs compact with finitely many affinoid ordinary interiors; its preimage is closed in their compact scalar extensions.

For a rational R_L with |f_i|≤r_i|g| and no common zero, let δ=min max(|g|,r_i^−1|f_i|)>0 on the ambient compact affinoid. Approximate g,f_i at one finite stage with errors <δ and <r_iδ. When |g|≥δ, denominator norm is unchanged; each numerator at or above its threshold has unchanged norm, while one below stays strictly below. Thus weak/strict comparisons and equality boundaries are unchanged. When |g|<δ some weighted numerator is ≥δ, stays unchanged, and makes both full systems false for the approximants too. This proves equality of the entire rational domain and its strict locus, including every equality locus within the validity domain; it does not falsely assert preservation of irrelevant individual equalities outside it. Surjectivity makes the approximants have no common zero downstairs, hence generate the unit ideal. The universal analytic-domain property identifies R_L=(R_E)_L with its ACTUAL rational algebra. The strict locus O_E is ordinary open and has full inverse image precisely O_L. These specific presentation neighborhoods, not arbitrary absolute interiors, are the needed ordinary interiors. Rational-neighborhood bases place them inside any given upstairs description open.

On such a compact R_L inside a form-description open, approximate each unit f_j by u_j from one finite R_E with Banach error <min|f_j|. Then |u_j|=|f_j| EXACTLY on all R_L. Surjectivity implies u_j is an actual unit on R_E, and the finite-stage moment image equals the upstairs moment image, so the same Euclidean coefficient domain is valid. The smooth scalar logarithm of f_j/u_j is numerical zero, hence the zero SECTION by compact-image nullity. Applying each derivation identifies both d't_fj and d''t_fj with the corresponding pulled-back unit differentials. Substitution in every term ω_IJ(t_f)d't_f,I∧d''t_f,J produces a stage form b_E with β=q_E*b_E on the entire saturated ordinary open, including zero regions. This is exact all-bidegree descent, not C0 approximation of differentiated forms.

Cover compact supp β by finitely many such saturated opens, enlarge to one finite E, and apply a compact partition θ_i at E near q_E(supp β), with supports compactly contained in their definition opens. Put α_E=∑ zero-extension(θ_i b_i,E). Each extension is ordinary smooth because its support is a compact closed subset inside the open. On the WHOLE upstairs space its pullback is (∑q_E*θ_i)β=β: the sum is one near supp β and β is zero elsewhere. No original-support saturation or stage-overlap agreement is assumed. Compact support is a finite union of cutoff supports. This explicitly proves arbitrary higher-form compact gluing rather than importing it from a scalar lemma.

INDEPENDENT PURITY AT COMPLETION. Fix y upstairs and a strict downstairs affinoid neighborhood V of its image. Total scalar dimension n gives local dimension at most n. If local dimension were m<n, remove from V_L every minimal component of dimension >m; none contains y. Choose a rational R_L of y inside the remaining ordinary open and inside the inverse image of int_X(V), with strict inequalities at y. The primary component/domain formula gives dim R_L≤m. Exact rational descent gives a nonempty R_E at one finite stage. Surjectivity puts it inside actual X_E, which is already pure n. Domain invariance gives dim R_E=n even if its auxiliary rational radii are non-strict; complete scalar dimension invariance gives dim R_L=dim R_E=n, contradiction. Every upstairs local dimension is n. For every minimal prime Q in an upstairs strict affinoid, a point with kernel Q lies on that component alone and proves dim(A_L/Q)=n. Thus EVERY upstairs component is checked. No simultaneous Noether normalization, unproved flat completed tensor injection, or total-dimension-only purity inference is needed. Goodness, strictness, separatedness and boundarylessness were separately checked by actual presentations, diagonals, and the primary boundary theorem.

Finally, for arbitrary complementary β=q_E*α_E, smooth differentiation gives Dβ=q_E*Dα_E. Both actual stages are pure n, supports are compact, and h is bounded there. Canonical top-measure projection yields

    B_hL(β)=∫(h_E∘q_E)(q_E*Dα_E)_Rad,L
           =∫h_E(Dα_E)_Rad,E=B_hE(α_E)=0.

This proves ascent; pulling back any compact downstairs α and using the same identity proves descent. Actual Artinian lengths are accounted for explicitly: for a finite Artinian C-algebra R of dimension d and any complete C'/C, R⊗C C' decomposes into local R_j with

    d=∑dim_C'(R_j)=∑length_Rj(R_j)[κ_j:C'].

Tensoring a basis and composition series prove this identity without separability or reducedness. These are the moment-fibre degrees in the primary calibration proof, so no field-degree or reduction normalization is inserted. Same-carrier restriction instead composes with the finite-flat torus map of rank [F:K].

Relative to the supplied residual scope, this adds the missing completed-algebraic CURRENT gate on arbitrary pure singular and nonreduced strict germs, without coordinate-product, invariant, PL, factorization, or imposed-upstairs-current hypotheses. It does not prove the original recognition target. Ordinary two-sign regularization or another legitimate general recognition bridge, arbitrary curve-map pullback, and general transcendental-extension current ascent remain unproved. P05.2 is untouched. The non-strict arbitrary-radius negative example does not provide an original-scope counterexample here.

to the original curve; the resulting function is classically pluriharmonic, locally R-PL, and
GJR harmonic. This does not supply locally twisted annular coordinates at the top or insert
annular stages at arbitrary intermediate levels of the tower.
     Annular geometry may also occur at the bottom. The general transfer statement Book
Proposition M.1.34 isolates the common exact descent, classical-pluriharmonic transfer, R-
harmonic transfer, and ﬁrst-current-rigidity transfer of the four allowed bundle types over an
arbitrary admissible base. Applying it to a globally coordinated curve-polyannulus product
gives Book Corollary M.1.53: after any such mixed tower, the top function still has the
unique logarithmic coeﬃcient formula over the original curve. Applying it instead to a locally
trivial curve-polyannulus bundle or a locally trivial mixed curve-polycylinder bundle gives
Book Corollary M.1.54, Book Corollary M.1.55, with classical pluriharmonicity, local R-PL
regularity, and GJR harmonicity but no global coeﬃcient formula. Thus locally twisted
annular coordinates are now allowed at the bottom of the mixed exact tower. The result
still requires their displayed analytic local trivializations and does not allow an annular stage
to be interleaved at an arbitrary later level, an annular ﬁbration without such charts, or an
arbitrary nonproduct germ.
     For globally coordinated annular products, the two endpoint orders can be fully interleaved.
In Book Theorem M.1.20, each stage of a ﬁnite boundaryless tower over the curve may be
either one of the four exact bundle types or a globally coordinated ﬁnite standard strict
open-polyannulus product. An induction preserves classical pluriharmonicity, R-harmonicity,
and ﬁrst-current rigidity at every level. It gives a unique normal form on the tower top
with one logarithmic term for every annular coordinate introduced anywhere in the tower;
the zero-current base coeﬃcient and all locally constant slope coeﬃcients live on the original
curve. Thus globally coordinated annular stages may now occur at arbitrary levels. For a
global normal form, the remaining obstruction is the transition monodromy of locally twisted
annulus bundles: the theorem does not choose global annular coordinates. For one locally
trivial polyannulus bundle over the curve, however, Book Proposition M.1.26 now identiﬁes the
coeﬃcient system on overlaps. The logarithmic coordinates transform by a locally constant
unimodular integer matrix and a vector of zero-current base functions. These data satisfy
the aﬃne cocycle law, deﬁne a rank-s local system of lattices, and make the local slope
vectors of every zero-current function a global parallel section of its dual real local system.
Thus the monodromy defect is encoded intrinsically even when it is not trivialized. The
remaining translation defect is measured exactly by the zero-current radiance class of Book
Deﬁnition M.1.1. Book Proposition M.1.27 makes its vanishing equivalent to a purely linear
overlap law after zero-current aﬃne gauge and then gives one global coeﬃcient formula for
every zero-current function. The gauges are not asserted to be logarithms of analytic units,
so this criterion does not manufacture global annular coordinates. Even when the full class
does not vanish, Book Proposition M.1.28 gives the exact residual answer slope by slope: the
slopes of global zero-current functions are precisely the parallel dual sections whose scalar
contraction with the radiance class vanishes. Its exact sequence also shows that an injective
contraction, and in particular the absence of parallel dual sections, forces unique descent of
every zero-current function to the original curve. When the radiance class vanishes, a chosen
aﬃne gauge splits this sequence.

     For the three regularity conclusions, part of that monodromy obstruction can be removed.
In Book Corollary M.1.33, one analytic open cover of the original curve is allowed to coordinate
every annular stage after base change. On each member of the cover, the whole restricted
tower is an instance of the interleaved theorem; the local conclusions therefore glue even
though the annular coordinates, radii, and product trivializations need not agree on overlaps.
Thus curve-controlled locally twisted annular stages may occur at arbitrary levels. The result
deliberately gives no global coeﬃcient formula. It also does not treat annular trivializations
available only over arbitrary opens of intermediate tower levels, because such opens need not
retain the preceding tower or its paracompactness hypotheses.

standard strict endpoint polycylinder and the ﬁbre is a locally trivial standard strict open
polydisc, then Book Proposition M.1.37 pulls every full zero-current function back from the
explicit aﬃne combination of the base annular logarithms. Thus it is classically pluriharmonic,
locally R-PL, and GJR harmonic. This allows open, closed, and half-closed annuli in the base,

tower of the displayed locally trivial strict open-polydisc bundles: Book Corollary M.1.56
ﬁrst descends the function to the endpoint-polycylinder base and then applies the endpoint
classiﬁcation. Each level must carry the stated local product charts; the nontrivial tower
result retains the formula together with local R-PL and GJR harmonicity, by propagating its
local curve-product charts. This still does not cover annular ﬁbres or ﬁbrations without them.
     There is a further invariant nonproduct range. Let the base be a good, topologically sepa-
rated, strict, pure positive-dimensional open inverse image in the extended tropicalization of
a split toric variety, and let a locally trivial standard strict open-polydisc bundle carry a lift
of its maximal compact torus action. If the continuous zero-current function is invariant for
that lifted action, then Book Corollary M.1.63 ﬁrst descends it to an invariant zero-current
function on the toric base and then applies the split-toric boundary theorem. It is therefore
locally real-PL, Gubler–Jell–Rabinoﬀ harmonic, and classically pluriharmonic. The action,
invariance, and actual local open-polydisc trivializations are hypotheses: this supplies no con-

## Result and scope

Let K be a complete nontrivially valued non-Archimedean field, let E/K be
any finite Galois extension, and let X be a good, separated, strict,
boundaryless K-analytic space, pure of dimension n >= 1. Retain the actual
analytic structure of X, including its nilpotents. Let h: X -> R be finite

proved below is

\[
 d'd''[h]=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad d'd''[h\circ\pi]=0.       \tag{T}
\]

(n-1,n-1)-forms. The respective canonical CLD calibrations are used. No
ramification, residue-characteristic, perfectness, normality, reducedness,
unit separation, Radon-Hessian, or invariant-form-descent hypothesis is
imposed. All open sets, neighborhoods, and supports below use the ordinary
Hausdorff topology. An affinoid neighborhood contains an ordinary open
neighborhood; this interior is not its absolute analytic interior.

This is a scalar-current transport theorem, not recognition of a general
continuous zero-current function as classically pluriharmonic. It establishes

It does not establish two-sign regularization, ascent through the completion

\[
 B_h(\alpha):=\int_X h\,(D\alpha)_{\mathrm{Rad},K}=0

## 1. Actual finite tensors, fibres, and component dimensions

### 1.0. Elementary field facts used in the construction

For completeness, no primitive-element or fixed-field result is hidden
in the induction. A finite separable extension L/K of an infinite field
has [L:K] embeddings into an algebraic closure: along a finite generating
tower, each existing embedding extends in exactly as many ways as the
degree of the next separable minimal polynomial, by choosing its distinct
roots. If a1,...,aq generate L, choose theta=sum_j c_j a_j so all these
embeddings give distinct values of theta. This is possible: each pair of
embeddings forbids a nonzero linear equation on (c_j); putting
(c_j)=(1,t,...,t^{q-1}) makes each forbidden equation a nonzero polynomial
in t, so finitely many forbidden roots cannot exhaust infinite K. The
minimal polynomial of theta has at least [L:K] distinct roots and degree
at most [L:K], hence L=K[theta]. Our K is infinite because a finite field
cannot have a nontrivial absolute value.

For normal separable E/K, every embedding of an intermediate field
extends to an embedding of E by the same successive-root construction;
normality puts the image back in E. Thus all such embeddings extend to
G. A G-fixed element has only one K-conjugate, so is in K: E^G=K.
For a subgroup H, put F=E^H and choose a K-primitive b for E. Then
E=F[b], and the product of T-hb over H has coefficients in F. Every
hb is a distinct root of the F-minimal polynomial of b, whereas that
minimal polynomial divides the product. Its degree is |H|, proving
E/F is Galois with group H. F/K is finite separable as a subextension
of E/K. For any embedding tau:F->E, its extension g in G identifies
the stage E/tau(F) with the conjugate subgroup gHg^{-1}.

### 1.1. Finite-module topology and invariants

For a K-affinoid Banach algebra A and a finite extension E/K of degree m,

\[
 A\widehat\otimes_K E=A\otimes_K E.                          \tag{4}
\]

Here is the topology justification. A fixed basis of a finite-dimensional
normed vector space over a complete valued field identifies its norm with
a norm equivalent to the coefficient maximum norm. Induct on dimension:
the span of all but the last basis vector is complete, hence closed; the
last vector has positive distance from it. Scaling that distance bounds
its coefficient in a vector; the ultrametric inequality and induction
bound the remaining coefficients. The upper bound follows directly from
the triangle inequality. Thus all coordinate maps E->K are bounded.
Tensor them with A. The tensor-norm upper bound in the other direction
identifies the topology on A tensor E with that on the finite direct sum
A^m. This direct sum is complete, proving (4). This proof is for the
actual algebra; no quotient by its nilradical occurs.

For G=Gal(E/K), the action 1 tensor g on (4) is bounded. The linear
equations (g-1)v=0 on E have common kernel K. Tensoring this finite kernel
calculation with a K-vector space is exact; hence

\[
 (A\otimes_K E)^G=A.                                       \tag{5}
\]

No averaging in characteristic p is used. In particular, an invariant
unit, together with its invariant inverse, is a unit of A. For every
unit f of A tensor E,

\[
N(f)=\prod_{g\in G}g f\in A^\times.                         \tag{6}
\]

For clarity, the point action and the translates of unit domains used
later are analytic on the restricted K-carrier: (4) is finite over A,
so foundation A makes it a K-affinoid algebra, and 1 tensor g is a
bounded K-algebra automorphism. Its K-spectrum is the same as its
E-spectrum because every seminorm restricts to the unique valued-field
norm on E. The actual rational algebras and their unit germs agree.
In particular |g f(y)|=|f(g^{-1}y)|. No invariance of a continuous
current or semilinear averaging of forms is used.

### 1.2. Analytic fibres and their decomposition groups

Let x belong to X, put C=H(x), and choose y above it. By (4) the actual
analytic fibre is M(C tensor_K E). A primitive element b for the finite
separable extension E/K identifies this algebra with C[T]/P(T), where
P is separable. Its factorization is a finite product of fields; each
factor is a finite complete valued extension of C and has one analytic
point. The uniqueness of its extending absolute value can be checked
without residue assumptions: two such values are equivalent norms on the
finite C-vector space, so comparison on z^r followed by r-th roots makes
them equal. Existence and completeness follow from the finite affinoid
field construction and the same finite-dimensional norm argument.

The G action is transitive on these factors. Otherwise the sum of the
idempotents of one orbit would be a nontrivial invariant idempotent, in
contradiction with (C tensor E)^G=C. Let H be the actual stabilizer of y
and let D_y be its field factor. Invariant tuples in the transitive
product are equivalent to H-invariant elements of D_y; therefore

\[
 D_y^H=C.                                                   \tag{7}
\]

The map E->D_y is injective. The image of b has |H| distinct H-conjugates,
and D_y=C[b]. The polynomial product over those conjugates has coefficients
in (7); the minimal polynomial of b over C divides it and has every one
of those distinct conjugates as a root. Its degree is consequently exactly
|H|. This proves directly that D_y/C is Galois with group H. In particular
the image of the finite separable field

\[
 F=E^H                                                     \tag{8}
\]

lies in C. If y is not fixed by all of G, H is proper and |H|<|G|.
This is a statement about the actual point and its fibre, not a
topological covering assertion.

### 1.3. Purity, strictness, and ordinary topology

Strict affinoid presentations base change to strict ones. Inverse images
of ordinary affinoid interiors give goodness upstairs; separatedness is
preserved by base change of the closed diagonal, and boundarylessness
follows from foundation B. The same assertions hold for ordinary opens.

We check every minimal component, not just total dimension. In a strict
affinoid neighborhood M(A) of a pure n-dimensional space, each minimal
prime P has dim(A/P)=n: by spectral surjectivity a point of kernel P
exists, belongs to that component alone, and its local dimension is n.
Let J be the nilradical. It is nilpotent. The injection

\[
 A/J\longrightarrow\prod_{P\text{ minimal}}\operatorname{Frac}(A/P)
\]

remains injective on tensoring with E. Each field tensor is reduced by
separability, so (A/J) tensor E is reduced. The nilradical of A tensor E
is exactly J tensor E. The kernels of the finitely many maps of this
reduced tensor algebra to those field factors are primes whose
intersection is zero. A minimal prime Q contains their product and hence
one of them; minimality makes it that kernel. Its contraction is its
associated P. The finite integral injection

\[
 A/P\hookrightarrow (A\otimes_K E)/Q
\]

preserves dimension. For clarity, this last elementary fact follows from
lying over, going up, and incomparability: for a finite integral injection
of domains C0->D0, localizing at p gives a nonzero finite C0_p-module.
If pD0_p=D0_p, the determinant of I minus a p-valued generator matrix
is a unit annihilating it, a contradiction. A maximal ideal over pD0_p
proves lying over. Apply the same argument after quotienting by a prime
to get going up. For incomparability, quotient by the smaller prime and
localize by the nonzero elements of the base domain. The resulting
finite integral domain over a field is a field: a minimum-degree monic
relation for a nonzero element expresses its inverse using its nonzero
constant term. Thus two strictly nested primes cannot have the same
contraction. Chain contraction and chain lifting prove dimension equality.

Every minimal component upstairs therefore has dimension n, and the
local dimension formula proves purity. Reduction was used only in this
dimension calculation, not in any current, unit, or calibration step.

Inverse images of compact sets under pi are compact. Indeed a downstairs
compact set is covered by finitely many ordinary interiors of affinoid
neighborhoods. Its inverse image is closed in the finite union of their
compact scalar extensions. Hausdorffness ensures that the closedness
statements here are ordinary topological statements.

We will repeatedly use a full-fibre shrinking observation. Inside an
affinoid neighborhood V0 of x, let N be an ordinary open in V0_E containing
the entire fibre over x. The compact complement has a closed image in V0
not containing x. Choose a smaller strict affinoid neighborhood V of x
inside that image's complement and inside the ordinary interior of V0.
Then V_E is contained in N. Its ordinary interior gives the corresponding
ordinary downstairs neighborhood. This retains any finite collection of
unit or strict norm conditions holding on the whole fibre.

## 2. A separable residue constant lifts to an actual neighborhood

K-embedding F->H(x) is given at a point of a good strict K-space. There
is a strict affinoid neighborhood V of x and a bounded embedding
F->O(V) whose evaluation is the specified embedding. Its restriction to
an ordinary neighborhood U of x makes U an F-analytic space on the same
carrier and with the same actual analytic function sheaf.

an inequality |b|>=|k0| strictly satisfied at x, with k0 in K^*. This
turns g into an actual analytic element. The following choices are
made before the final shrink.

0<d<|P'(a)|. Put

\[

\]

\[

\]

a sufficiently closely that |g(x)|<R, |P'(g)(x)|>d,
|P(g)(x)|<c and also |g(x)-a|<s. Preserve these strict inequalities
on the strict rational domain defined by

\[
 |g|\leq R,\quad |P(g)|\leq c,\quad |P'(g)|\geq d.            \tag{11}
\]

g/R, P(g)/c, and d/P'(g). The last relation makes P'(g) invertible
as an actual algebra element. Its quotient Banach norm has

\[

              \|P'(g)^{-1}\|\leq d^{-1}.                    \tag{12}
\]

These bounds arise from relations in the quotient algebra and remain
valid in the presence of nilpotents. We have not inferred a Banach bound
from the spectral seminorm.

## 6. The full tensor collar estimate, including boundary-face contact

Here is the elementary estimate needed for (20).

**Collar lemma.** Let Q be a fixed linear map on a Euclidean space V
with kernel W; an orthogonal projection may be used. Let sigma be a
compact n-dimensional affine polytope. Let xi be a smooth (n-1,n-1)
superform on a neighborhood of sigma and of the nearby W points, with
i^*xi=0 on W. Take a fixed smooth radial function chi on Q(V), equal
to one near zero and supported in the unit ball, and define

\[
 \xi_\delta(z)=\chi(Qz/\delta)\xi(z),\quad 0<\delta\leq1.
\]

On sigma, the coefficient L1 norms of D xi_delta are uniformly bounded
as delta tends to zero. The coefficient L1 norm of xi_delta tends to zero.
These conclusions still hold with arbitrary fixed constant cell volume
and with additional Euclidean coordinates on which Q is zero. Only the
restriction of the superforms to the affine tangent of sigma is measured.

**Proof.** Let L be the n-dimensional tangent plane of sigma and put
r=rank(Q|L). If its affine span misses W, the affine image Q(span sigma)
is a closed affine subspace not containing zero, at positive distance
from it. For sufficiently small delta the collar is empty. Otherwise
choose w0 in that affine span intersect W and write z=w0+u+v, with
u in L intersect W and v in a fixed complement L1 of dimension r.
Q|L1 is an isomorphism to its image. Compactness bounds u in one fixed
box, and |Qz|<=delta bounds v in a box of side O(delta). Fubini and the
fixed determinant give collar volume O(delta^r). This argument does not
require w0+u to belong to sigma: it works for a cell meeting W only at a
boundary face, or with zero-dimensional intersection. If a compact cell
itself misses W, its distance is positive and the same conclusion follows.

For r=0 a cell intersecting W lies in W. Its xi restriction is identically
zero, so the restriction of D xi_delta is also identically zero. For
r>=2, cutoff derivatives of orders j=0,1,2 are O(delta^-j) on the fixed
cell, and xi and its first two coefficient derivatives are bounded.
The Leibniz expansion therefore bounds D xi_delta by O(delta^-2).
Multiplying by O(delta^r) gives a uniform integral bound.

For r=1 write the affine tangent coordinates as (u1,...,u_{n-1},t),
with z=w0+u+t v and v fixed, Qv nonzero. The cutoff restricted to this
plane depends only on t and has derivatives O(delta^-1) and
O(delta^-2). Expand the restricted xi in the exterior basis using
d'u_j,d't and d''u_j,d''t. There is exactly one possible basis monomial
of bidegree (n-1,n-1) containing neither d't nor d''t:

\[
 A(u,t)\,d'u_1\wedge\cdots\wedge d'u_{n-1}
          \wedge d''u_1\wedge\cdots\wedge d''u_{n-1}.         \tag{22}
\]

Its coefficient A(u,0) is zero, because the u-plane at t=0 is tangent
to W and i^*xi=0 there. Smoothness on a fixed compact neighborhood gives
|A(u,t)|<=C|t|. The comparison point w0+u can lie outside the cell;
it is still on W and within O(delta) of its compact collar. This is
exactly why restriction-zero is needed on the ambient W, not just at
points of sigma intersect W.

The second-cutoff term is chi''(t) d't wedge d''t wedge xi. Every
monomial of xi containing at least one transverse generator is annihilated
by a repeated exterior generator. Only (22) remains, bounded by
O(delta^-2) O(delta)=O(delta^-1) on the collar. All first-cutoff terms
are O(delta^-1), since their other coefficients and derivatives are
bounded. The term chi D xi is bounded. The collar volume is O(delta),
so all differentiated terms have bounded coefficient L1 norm. This
includes n=1: then (22) is just the scalar coefficient, vanishing on W.

For the undifferentiated form, coefficients are bounded and every
positive-rank collar has volume tending to zero; rank-zero cells either
miss the collar or give the zero restriction. A finite number of cells,
fixed coordinate Jacobians, and fixed positive calibration constants do
not change either conclusion. **End of proof.**

This lemma is not a claim that a small collar gives small differentiated
variation; the latter is only bounded and need not tend to zero. Rank one
uses both exterior-tensor cancellation and the first-order vanishing in
(22). No balanced-fan recognition theorem or curve probe is involved.

### 6.1. From coefficient bounds to actual top-measure variation

On a compact affinoid moment chart of dimension n, foundation E gives a
finite polyhedral image and a finite skeletal n-cell refinement. Above
each image cell sigma, the finitely many skeletal cells map by affine
isomorphisms and have positive constant calibration d_C times a primitive
volume. For an ambient top form zeta, its density on each such sheet is
the same affine-tangent scalar density, multiplied by that positive
constant. Thus taking absolute values before summing gives

\[
 \|(t^*\zeta)_{\mathrm{Rad}}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \leq\sum_{\sigma} c_\sigma
        \int_\sigma\|\zeta|_{T\sigma}\|\,d\operatorname{vol}_\sigma,
                                                                  \tag{23}
\]

for fixed finite c_sigma. In an oriented tangent basis the scalar-density
version is an equality; the norm inequality allows arbitrary bases.
There is no signed cancellation hidden in this bound. It is the local
construction in CLD 5.8.4-5 plus 14.3.2 and 14.5.2, not an inference
from signed pushforward equality alone. The constants include all actual
finite-flat fibre dimensions, and therefore all nilpotent lengths.
Cells below dimension n contribute zero. If the whole moment image has
dimension <n, every represented top form is zero. We never replace that
case by an assumed universal dimension equality.

Finitely many such compact charts covering a fixed ordinary compact
support suffice. Top measures restrict compatibly to domains; overcounting
their positive variations in an overlapping cover yields an upper bound.
No derivative of a partition is needed to obtain (23).

## 7. Weak convergence on the full continuous multiplier

Fix a gamma=gamma_i from (20), its orbit moment t, and put Q=1-P0.
Choose the radial chi of section 6 and define, in its chart and extended
by zero,

\[
 e_\delta=\chi(Qt/\delta)\gamma.                            \tag{24}
\]

These are ordinary smooth complementary tests with supports in the
same compact C. The compact test (1-chi(Qt/delta)) gamma has support
disjoint from S: on S, Qt=0 and the multiplier equals zero on an ordinary
neighborhood. Section 3 therefore gives the **exact** identity

\[
 B_{h_E}(\gamma)=B_{h_E}(e_\delta)\quad(\delta>0).             \tag{25}
\]

Cover C by finitely many strict affinoid neighborhoods contained in the
chart, and add moment coordinates for local descriptions of the fixed
downstairs cutoff theta_i. On each enlarged ambient space, gamma is a
smooth coefficient form whose restriction to W times the extra space
vanishes. The collar lemma, (23), and the finite cover give

\[
 \sup_{0<\delta\leq\delta_0}
       \|(D e_\delta)_{\mathrm{Rad},E}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}<\infty. \tag{26}
\]

The constant may depend on this test and this compact carrier. It is
independent of delta. This is a statement about smooth differentiated
forms, not a Radon regularity hypothesis on D[h_E].

Let a be any fixed ordinary smooth compact scalar multiplier. Stokes
twice, on the boundaryless pure space X_E, gives

\[
 \int_{X_E}a\,D e_\delta=\int_{X_E}e_\delta\wedge D a.        \tag{27}
\]

For explicit signs, 0=integral d'(a d''e) says integral aDe=
-integral d'a wedge d''e. Next 0=integral d''(d'a wedge e) says
integral d'a wedge d''e=integral d''d'a wedge e=-integral Da wedge e.
The total degree of e is even, so Da wedge e=e wedge Da. These
calculations require no symmetry of e and thus treat every ordinary
complementary test.

To show the right side tends to zero, add **the moment coordinates
describing a** on a finite compact chart cover of C. This additional
refinement is essential: L1 information on a smaller moment need not
by itself control a wedge with Da. The enlarged fixed subspace is
W times all the added coordinates, and the coefficient restriction of
gamma still vanishes there. The undifferentiated conclusion of the
collar lemma gives L1 convergence to zero on every calibrated n-cell of
this enlarged moment; Da has bounded coefficients on the fixed compact
images. Formula (23) applied to e_delta wedge Da proves

\[
 \int a\,(D e_\delta)_{\mathrm{Rad},E}\longrightarrow0.       \tag{28}
\]

The refinement and constants for (28) may depend on a. They do not need
to be uniform in a. Uniformity in delta for (26), already obtained
without a, is what the continuous passage uses.

Approximate h_E on C within epsilon by an ordinary smooth compact a
using section 4. If M is the bound in (26), then

\[
 \limsup_{\delta\to0}
 \left|\int h_E\,(D e_\delta)_{\mathrm{Rad},E}\right|
 \leq M\varepsilon.                                       \tag{29}
\]

Let epsilon tend to zero. Equations (25) and (29) imply B_{h_E}(gamma)=0.
